summary: An excerpt from a fiction text in which Rebecca brings the Simpson baby home from the farm for a Sunday visit, but Miss Miranda refuses to let the baby stay. Rebecca then complains to aunt Jane, who is sorting linens upstairs, about her disappointment. Rebecca decides to take the baby home in the soap-wagon and changes the baby's petticoat. The note also contains an odd inserted line attributed to Stuart about being lactose intolerant.
one_line: Excerpt from a fiction book where Rebecca, refused permission to keep a borrowed baby over Sunday, takes her home and dresses her.
key_facts: Rebecca brought the Simpson baby home so she could do her Saturday work while looking after the baby.
Miss Miranda tells Rebecca to give the child some supper and carry it home where it belongs.
Miss Miranda refuses to let the borrowed baby stay for the weekend.
Mrs. Simpson was planning to go to Milltown, and Rebecca says she will be dreadfully disappointed.
Emma Jane has the promise of the baby's next Sunday, and Alice Robinson has the one after that.
Mrs. Simpson wanted Rebecca to have the baby first because Rebecca has so much experience with babies.
The baby has yellow hair and big blue eyes, and Mrs. Simpson says she takes after her father.
Miss Miranda says the baby's father would take anything there was before she got there.
Aunt Jane is in the upstairs linen closet sorting clean sheets and pillow cases for Saturday.
Rebecca says she wishes she had a printed book listing everything she could do, so she would not be disappointed so often.
Aunt Jane answers that no book could fit Rebecca because nobody could foresee the things she would want to do.
Rebecca plans to drag the baby home in the little soap-wagon instead of carrying her.
Rebecca removes a crooked pin from the baby's waistband and attaches her red flannel petticoat with a large safety pin.
The note includes a line reading 'I'm lactose intolerant,' attributed to Stuart, which does not fit the surrounding scene.
